name: walk
description: Walk — on-device footage triage for photographers. Scans video on Apple silicon and returns candidate frames with their measurements and a written thumbnail. Ships an MCP server; requires macOS 26 on arm64.

interface.shortDescription: Find the frames worth keeping in a folder of footage, measured on-device.
interface.longDescription: Walk decodes video on Apple silicon and finds the frames worth a second look: a whole-frame luminance-rise detector paired with an on-device Vision classifier, with every candidate carrying its frame index, timecode, the rise over a local median baseline, 10-bit Y-plane statistics, classifier confidences, and a written thumbnail you can open. The classification runs on the machine, so a clip of several thousand frames costs no tokens to look at. The measurements are evidence, not a ranking: a frame that scores badly can be the photograph, and sorting by brightness is how a first pass loses real events. Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon — the engine links Vision, CoreML and AVFoundation and has no Intel build and no port.
